title: GPU Health Heuristic Gallery for Dedicated Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, scan-friendly 'heuristic gallery' view for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health signals (thermal, utilization, KV cache pressure, GPU memory fragmentation), autoscale intent controls, and quick burst management. The gallery should serve both an on-call operator who needs rapid triage and a platform engineer who needs context for tuning autoscale rules. It must integrate with existing rollout controls and cost breakdown panels without adding visual clutter.
goals: Enable 30s surface-level triage: identify pools with thermal risk, cache thrashing, or overcommit
Provide one-click corrective actions (reduce burst, pin model variant, trigger scale-out) from the gallery
Bridge telemetry and cost: show estimated token-cost impact when toggling burst or adjusting batch windows
Fit into the Console's compact rows (height <= 120px) and be keyboard accessible
scope: New gallery row component for the Pools list + dedicated Pool detail header
Three primary tiles per pool: Health Sparkline, Autoscale Intent, Burst Credits
Hover inspector with expanded panel containing recent events and links to traces
Figma prototype + interactive handoff for front-end (React) and telemetry backend event shape
acceptance_criteria: Design reviewed and signed off by PM and Eng leads
Prototype demonstrates hover inspector, action buttons, and accessibility keyboard flows
Front-end has a clear token of fields to expect: {thermal: number, kv_hit_rate: number, burst_credits: number, p95_latency_ms: number} in Confluence spec
Usability test (N=6) shows operators can correctly prioritize pools 5/6 times within 90s
design_decisions: Use a compact three-band layout instead of a dense table column to reduce horizontal scroll
Represent thermal/temperature as a 10-level left-right heatbar (color + numeric tooltip) to avoid ambiguous color-only cues
Autoscale intent is expressed as an interactive micro-knob (0-100 scale) rather than a dropdown to make adjustments fast
Burst credits shown as radial micro-meter with small numeric delta; long-press opens burst edit dialog with duration presets
Progressive disclosure: only show KV cache pressure if >20% deviation from baseline to reduce noise
Cost estimates are local, optimistic projections (5-minute window) and include a small confidence band
tradeoffs_and_risks: Density vs legibility: compact rows save space but require hover for full context — risk for keyboard-only users mitigated with focus states
Estimated cost projection may be misinterpreted as billing guarantee; we will prefix with 'estimate' and link to cost explainer
Adding corrective actions in-UI increases blast radius; actions will require confirmation and role-checks (RBAC) enforced by backend
feedback_notes: 2025-02-14 - Olivia Nguyen (PM): Likes the gallery concept; asked for clearer mapping to rollout states and whether can trigger canary scale-outs directly
2025-02-20 - Diego Ramos (ENG): Concern about telemetry cardinality; requested that the design include a fallback empty-state that prompts for enabling 1m-sampled metrics
2025-03-03 - Priya Singh (SRE): Requested a 'snooze alerts' quick action and suggested 4 color-blind-safe palettes for heatbar
2025-03-10 - Legal/Compliance check (Anita Rao): No PII surfaced; asked to avoid sending full instance IDs to the client in hover payloads
mockup_versions: v0.2 - compact rows with hover inspector (2025-02-21)
usability_findings: Participants confused color-only heatbar on first glance; adding numeric overlay improved accuracy
Operators preferred micro-knob for autoscale intent because it avoids opening a modal for small tweaks
Burst edit modal needed clearer defaults; testers chose shorter durations unless presented with estimated cost impact
